0.original: Krile is eager to begin searching the research facility.

24.original: Search for a way to the upper floor.

28.original: Speak with Shale in the Backroom.

48.original: Teeshal Ja, you said her name was? I wonder what her story is...

49.original: Is it alright if I go around by myself now?

50.original: The villagers were likely monitoring the imprisoned tural vidraal at Zoraal Ja's behest. And at some point, they became involved in the research of souls...

51.original: Now that the danger is behind us, it's started sinking in just how unsettling this place is. Hard to believe it used to be a village.

52.original: It seems this Kanilokka was in charge here. From your recounting, he was quite dedicated to Zoraal Ja.

53.original: I'll launch the hover cargo whenever you're ready. Just say the word.

55.original: While we've discerned the purpose of the research conducted here, the traces of it that remain might afford us greater insight into what came of it.

56.original: Let us take a look around─for information as well as a way to the upper level.

57.original: It makes me angry to think about what they did here...

58.original: What happened to the people here? Did they all leave...or did we already meet them?

59.original: To think that people actually volunteered their souls for these experiments...

60.original: Success was far from guaranteed, and even in the best case, they would cease to be men. Was their devotion to Zoraal Ja so absolute?

61.original: It won't open, and I don't think it'll yield to our shoulders either. We'll have to do it the old-fashioned way and find the key.

62.original: The researchers likely moved between the upper and lower levels. Perhaps we can find a key among their belongings.

63.original: I wonder what Beq Lugg would make of this research into transferring souls.

64.original: A lift can be seen behind the wrought-iron gate. As sturdy as it appears, the gate will likely resist attempts to force it open.

65.original: A security panel is nearby. Perhaps a verification key will open the way.

66.original: A journal lies next to the body...

67.original: (-Researcher's Journal-)<hex:021A020203>I was transferred to Yuweyawata station in order to train the villagers in the use of electrope technology.<hex:021A020103>

68.original: (-Researcher's Journal-)<hex:021A020203>While a child can quickly learn to operate common contraptions, it will be no easy thing for them to attain the requisite skill to develop new weapons─ones which require no less than the manipulation of souls.<hex:021A020103>

69.original: (-Researcher's Journal-)<hex:021A020203>Thankfully, two of my pupils have demonstrated great aptitude in the field: Kanilokka, the village chief, and Teeshal Ja, a field chirurgeon.<hex:021A020103>

70.original: (-Researcher's Journal-)<hex:021A020203>Further driven by their loyalty to our king, their growth has been remarkable. I dare to hope that, before long, they will be able to carry out their duties without further instruction, and I may be relieved of my duty.<hex:021A020103>

71.original: You find nothing that resembles a verification key. Perhaps you should search elsewhere.

72.original: (-Test Subject's Journal-)<hex:021A020203>They're recruiting volunteers for a new experiment. I know I'm not as bright as the others, but they wouldn't laugh at me if I was stronger than them. This might be my chance.<hex:021A020103>

73.original: (-Test Subject's Journal-)<hex:021A020203>Soul transferred few days ago. I can write. Can write good, yes? I am good! Very good!<hex:021A020103>

74.original: (-Test Subject's Journal-)<hex:021A020203>Getting hard to control strength. Today bit off hand of feeder. Cannot help it so strong.<hex:021A020103>

75.original: (-Test Subject's Journal-)<hex:021A020203>Hungry. Always hungry. Cannot control. Eat. I must eat am eater must eat...<hex:021A020103>

76.original: Supplies for the staff are neatly arranged within the cabinet. Among the various items is a manual outlining regulations and tranquilizing gas to be used in emergencies. You dig deeper...

77.original: ...And find a verification key! Perhaps it can be used to open the iron gate.

79.original: You found the key? Great, I'll call the others.

80.original: It seems the key can be used to operate the lift as well. Up we go.

82.original: I didn't expect it to be similar, but this is a far cry from the temple that held Valigarmanda.

83.original: All the machinery appears to still be in operation. I expect there are auxiliary systems in place to ensure that monitoring can continue even in emergencies.

84.original: The warnings indicate various anomalies─related to the seal's failure, most likely. For a blessing, we managed to fell the beast before it could cause harm.

85.original: Right then, let's see if we can find some clues about Gulool Ja's mother.

86.original: I think I can use this terminal. Shale taught me how.

87.original: There's so much data... I don't know what we should look at.

88.original: Perhaps we can narrow down the search by inputting the name Teeshal Ja.

89.original: Ah, it brought up a lot of results. They all seem to say the same thing...

90.original: “Teeshal Ja, Administrator of Experimental Treatments: Research Logs.”

92.original: Chances are the data is encrypted. And even if not, it will take considerable time to go through it all.

93.original: Then let us take it with us to the Backroom and have Shale analyze it.

95.original: Alright. I'll transfer it to this storage device I brought.

97.original: Thank you so much for bringing me all the way here, everyone!

98.original: If you're happy, then so am I. Besides, I was able to learn more about my brother as well. It was a fruitful adventure for the both of us.

99.original: It seems safe to say my brother returned to Yuweyawata for the tural vidraal. He wanted its power, no matter the cost...

100.original: Kiluwsa is really good at driving the hover cargo. I wonder if I can learn how to drive it too...

101.original: I'll not soon forget our visit to that facility. It was a troubling reminder of the depravity that can arise from the belief that souls are simply a resource to be exploited.

102.original: I admit the tural vidraal gave me a fright at first. But then I remembered who felled the mighty Valigarmanda!

103.original: I'm glad we could find what we sought in that abandoned facility.

104.original: And here we are. The authorities will doubtless wish to be informed about the facility and its contents...

105.original: But first things first: let us deliver the data to Shale.

106.original: Gulool Ja had no trouble keeping up during the outing. He really is his father's son.

107.original: It was Shale who gave me the storage device before we left. She said that we'd probably need it...and we did!

108.original: Having now spent some time in these harsh environs, I feel I have a better understanding of how much of a steadying presence Sphene was to her people.

109.original: From what I can see, things haven't changed much since the funeral. People are still listless like before.

110.original: I've been thinking, it may behoove us to learn how to use the various devices found throughout Alexandria. Better late than never, after all.

111.original: The data will be in good hands with Shale.

112.original: You've found information on Gulool Ja's mother? You lot never cease to amaze...

113.original: Welcome back. Gulool Ja has already given me the storage device.

114.original: There looks to be a wealth of data, all of which is encrypted, so I'll need time to process everything.

115.original: In that case, Alisaie and I might take ourselves around the city and check on the people.

116.original: Aye, their mood has us a bit worried. I don't know if there's anything we can do to help, but we'll see...

117.original: Understood. I'll let you know as soon as I've finished my work.

118.original: Thank you. We'll see you again soon.
